messages:
Leah Gomez: Hi! Day 3 question: where should I post different onboarding problems (hardware, VPN, repo access)? Also, a coworker told me not to poke certain botswhat's the safe etiquette for bots and channels?
Connor Price: Welcome Leah! Quick map we use: hardware/shipping -> #people-ops (use the pinned form), VPN & infra creds -> #eng-infra, repo access -> open the SSO access ticket in #help and add your GitHub username.
Marta Silva: If it's blocking your work (no VPN or no repo access), post in #help and mention @eng-oncall or the person listed in the pinned message. That gets eyes fast. :exclamation:
Leah Gomez: Nice. And bots? I saw "fun-emoji" in #random and a deploy app in #eng-releases.
Connor Price: Rule of thumb: if a bot has "sandbox" or "test" in its description, it's safe to interact with in public; otherwise try commands in DM or in #dev-playground. Never run deploy or admin slash commands in public unless you're sure of the workflow.
Marta Silva: We also discourage invoking unknown slash commands in company-wide channels. If you want to test something, use #dev-playground or DM the bot; that prevents accidental noisy announcements.
OnboardBot: Hi Leah  you can re-run your checklist with `/onboard checklist`  I'll DM you the items. To view what was completed use `/onboard status`.
IT Helper: For hardware exchanges, open the ticket at https://peopleops.internal/tickets and include your manager and shipping address. If urgent, add "urgent: hardware" in the subject.
Leah Gomez: Good call. Any short etiquette bullets so I don't clog channels?
Connor Price: TL;DR: 1) Search the handbook and channel history first. 2) Pick the most specific channel (don't post "build failing" in #general). 3) Use threads for follow-ups. 4) Keep logs concise and use fenced code blocks for short snippets. 5) Never paste secrets in Slack; use the secret manager or DM and rotate if leaked.
Marta Silva: Example post for #eng: "@eng build failing on ubuntu-22.04, ran `make build`, last 6 lines below" + a fenced codeblock with the 6 relevant lines. For long traces, paste an unlisted gist and link it.
Leah Gomez: If I accidentally post a secret, what's the exact flow?
Connor Price: Delete the message immediately, rotate the secret, then ping #eng-security. There's a secrets-runbook pinned in #eng-security with steps and a contact for emergency rotations.
Marta Silva: Also note some channels are read-only (monitoring, deploy feeds). The channel header will say "read-only"  don't post there. If unsure, check channel purpose or ask an admin.
Leah Gomez: Perfect. I'll use #help for urgent stuff and #dev-playground to try bots. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
thread_notes: keeps mapping concise and points to sandbox channel for bot testing
